articles.title: Amanda Anisimova Weight Loss: Tennis Star Looks Unrecognizable After Serious Body Transformation
articles.summary: Amanda Anisimova's new training photos have been the talk of fitness, as the former World No. 3 strives to get back into her prime.
articles.body:
Amanda Anisimova has created shockwaves in the tennis world with her latest athletic transformation. Fans are discussing the visible difference in her physique as the American looks to make a much-awaited comeback in tennis competitions.

The 25-year-old has already shown her dominance in the tennis rankings by reaching a career-high No. 3 in 2026. This success happened after a very impressive 2025 campaign, which saw her reach the Grand Slam finals at Wimbledon and the US Open, and win WTA 1000 titles in Doha and Beijing.

Now, her weight loss is the talk of the town in the world of tennis.

Amanda Anisimova's Weight Loss Takes Centre Stage

New photos from Anisimova's training session have created a lot of buzz. The athletic tennis player practicing drills and her weight loss over some months have stunned the social media world.

Anisimova looks almost unrecognizable after her serious weight loss journey in 2026. The tennis star looks to make a stunning comeback this year.

Fitness has been a key element in Anisimova's growth over the years. Her high performance was directly related to her fitness levels, which resulted in an impressive 2025 campaign.

Her coach, Hendrik Vleeshouwers, had previously told us that they had done a lot of work on fitness to get Anisimova comfortable with playing long rallies and longer matches. Her fitness goals were to trust her body that would eventually help her tennis prowess to win vital games.

Anisimova also confessed that her physique helped her during matches, and she strove to maintain the same during the off-season.

Anisimova has been struggling for most of 2026. She suffered a wrist injury, which ended her clay-court season. Additionally, there was drama in her coaching changes as well. Anisimova had parted ways with coach Vleeshouwers in March. However, the 25-year-old reunited with her coach before the US Open this year.

Despite the rough patches of the season, the WTA still ranks Anisimova at No. 11.

Her most recent training photos, then, provide a snapshot of a player who continues to put a lot of effort into preparation. The change might have been noticed by the fans, but the next time Anisimova is on court, it will be best to see how far she has come.

articles.title: Nikolás Sánchez impulsa al tenis español al mejor balance challenger en ocho años
articles.standfirst: Su título en Szeczin es el número 23 del palmarés colectivo español
articles.summary: Su título en Szeczin es el número 23 del palmarés colectivo español
articles.body: El tenis español ha alcanzado, mediado septiembre, el vigésimo tercer título Challenger ATP, de los que 13 son individuales y 10 se han ganado en dobles. Se superan así los 22 éxitos de 2025 y 2026 se convierte en el año con más títulos challengers, el circuito en el que se forjan las promesas del futuro del tenis, desde 2018, donde se alcanzaron los 28 galardones. Se está a un solo título individual de igualar los 11 del año pasado. El título fue conseguido en el de Szczecin (Polonia), de categoría 125, por Nikolás Sánchez Izquierdo (segundo Challenger de su carrera), venciendo en la final al veterano brasileño Thiago Monteiro 4-6 6-3 7-6(6). Hasta la final no había cedido un set en todo el torneo. Además, final de dobles de Íñigo Cervantes y semifinales de Mario Mansilla y Benjamín Winter. Y en el 50 de Biella (Italia), final de Alejandro Moro y cuartos de final de Oriol Roca; en dobles, semifinales de Ignasi Forcano y Àlex Martí. En el circuito ITF, en el M25 de Sintra (Portugal), cuartos de final de John Echeverría. Y en el M15 de Melilla, semifinales de Alejandro Turriziani y Carles Córdoba y cuartos de final de Carles Rojas; en dobles, título de Carles Rojas (segundo) y semifinales de Luis García, Noah Regas, Mario Arce y Esteban Talavera. En el circuito WTA 125 Series, en el torneo de Valencia, final de Alicia Herrero y cuartos de Irene Burillo, Guiomar Maristany y Andrea Lázaro; en dobles, final de Irene Burillo y semifinales de Leyre Romero y Oksana Selekhmeteva. Por último, esta semana se ha celebrado la Copa del Mundo por equipos de tenis en silla, en el que España ha quedado en cuarto lugar, con un equipo formado por Martín de la Puente, Dani Caverzaschi y Kike Siscar.

articles.title: Alcaraz y Zverev hablan de la final del US Open: "Estaba viéndolo en casa y me quedé flipando"
articles.standfirst: El tenista murciano le preguntó al alemán por cómo no se pudo dar cuenta de que había ganado el partido
articles.summary: El tenista murciano le preguntó al alemán por cómo no se pudo dar cuenta de que había ganado el partido
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz ha mantenido una conversación con Alexander Zverev en la pista que acogerá a partir de este 25 de septiembre una nueva edición de la Laver Cup. El 02 Arena de Londres asistirá a un nuevo duelo entre Europa y el Resto del Mundo. El español y el alemán, que podrían verse las caras en las semifinales de la Copa Davis en Bolonia, hablaron distendidamente de lo sucedido en la final del US Open. Zverev conquistó su segundo grand slam sin ser consciente que lo había logrado. Tras anotarse el punto final ante Ben Shelton, se marchó a restar porque pensó que el marcador era 5-1. Alcaraz le recordó este lance a Zverev: "Dime en qué estabas pensando. Yo estaba viéndolo en casa y me quedé flipando". "No había nada en mi cabeza, cuando eres estúpido eso ayuda", respondió el alemán entre risas. La conversación siguió por este tono. "No, no digas eso, lo estuve pensando, te ayuda mucho no saber que es el último set", afirmó Alcaraz. Zverev le dio la razón: "Sí, yo pensaba que el marcador era 4-1, así que no me puse nervioso, si hubiera sabido que era 5-2 me habría puesto supernervioso"

articles.title: Tennis: British player Tara Moore's latest legal bid over doping ban dismissed by US court
articles.summary: British player Tara Moore's legal bid for £15m in damages over a doping case which led to her being banned for four years is dismissed.
articles.body:
British doubles player Tara Moore's legal bid for £15m ($20m) in damages from the Women's Tennis Association - over a doping case which led to her being banned for four years - has been dismissed by a United States court.

Moore, 34, argued the WTA - the governing body of the women's tour - failed to warn players about the risk of eating contaminated meat at a tournament held in Colombia.

But the United States District Court in New York has dismissed Moore's motion and directed to "close this matter".

Moore, who has always denied intentionally doping, told BBC Sport after the ruling that the case has been a "nightmare".

"It just shows how broken the anti-doping system is in tennis," Moore said.

Keothavong 'can't fault' GB after BJK Cup loss to Czechs

GB dominate Ecuador to reach Davis Cup Finals

In April 2022, Moore tested positive for nandrolone and boldenone at a WTA 250 event in Bogota, with an independent tribunal ruling in December 2023 that contaminated meat was the source.

Moore, who was Britain's leading women's doubles player at the time of the failed test, was found to bear "no fault or negligence", but the International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA) appealed against the decision.

Last year, the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas) ruled in favour of the ITIA and Moore was banned until 2028.

Moore then initiated proceedings with the American Arbitration Association, in which she claimed the WTA's "failure to warn against eating meat in Colombia was a direct cause of her positive test result and the harm that followed".

The arbitrator supported the ruling made by Cas and dismissed the case against the WTA.

In response, Moore filed a motion against the decision at the United States District Court in New York.

Moore, who was ranked a career-high 77th in the world in 2022, claimed she was denied a fair hearing by the arbitrator.

The motion detailed how Moore was seeking "no less than $20m in compensatory damages" after claiming the WTA "stayed silent in the face of a known and specific danger and then shifted the blame for its own negligence" to the player.

On Friday, United States district judge Andrew Carter found Moore's challenge was "not justified" on a legal basis.

The WTA and ITIA have been approached for comment.

articles.title: Desestiman la demanda de 20 millones de Tara Moore contra la WTA
articles.standfirst: Pedía la cantidad por supuestas irregularidades en suspensión por dopaje
articles.summary: Pedía la cantidad por supuestas irregularidades en suspensión por dopaje
articles.body: La demanda por valor de 20 millones de dólares (17,5 millones de euros) que la tenista Tara Moore, sancionada cuatro años por dopaje, puso contra la WTA, ha sido desestimada por un juez en Nueva York. Moore, que llegó a ser la mejor británica en dobles, dio un doble positivo en esteroides en 2022 y alegó que fue debido al consumo de carne contaminada en Colombia. Pese a que recibió una suspensión temporal y estuvo 19 meses fuera de competición, su sanción fue revocada por un tribunal independiente. Pero la ITIA, el organismo que vela por la integridad en el tenis, llevó el caso al Tribunal de Arbitraje Deportivo que corroboró la sanción de cuatro años. Esto desembocó en que Moore llevó el incidente a arbitraje con la WTA primero y, tras fallar esta vía, demandó a la asociación tenística en Estados Unidos. La defensa de Moore se basó en que la WTA no proveyó de suficiente información a las jugadoras sobre los riesgos de comer carne en determinados países. Sin embargo, el juez Andrew Carter determinó que no había base legal para la demanda de Moore y que el proceso de arbitraje había sido justo. La suspensión de Moore, que ahora tiene 34 años, terminará en diciembre de 2027.

articles.title: Jay Meena scripts history, assures India’s first Asian Games soft tennis medal
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: India’s Jay Meena scripted history at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games on Wednesday, reaching the men’s singles semi-finals and assuring the country of it.
articles.body: India’s Jay Meena scripted history at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games on Wednesday, reaching the men’s singles semi-finals and assuring the country of its first-ever Asian Games medal in soft tennis.Playing in his third Asian Games, Meena battled past the Philippines’ Sherwin Nuguit in a seven-game quarter-final thriller, winning 4-3 to book his place in the last four.Asian Games Full Coverage | Schedule | Medal TallyThe Indian recovered from a tough start to eventually prevail 0-4, 4-2, 2-4, 5-3, 2-4, 7-5 in a closely fought contest against Nuguit.Meena’s semi-final berth guarantees him a medal, marking a landmark achievement for Indian soft tennis at the Asian Games. He had previously competed at the 2018 and 2022 editions of the Games.The 4-3 victory capped a strong run for Meena, who had earlier defeated Pakistan’s Arain Hussain 4-0 in the men’s singles Group D to progress to the quarter-finals.Meena will now take on the semi-finals with a chance to go a step further and secure a place in the gold medal match.India also added a bronze medal in the women’s skeet team event, with Raiza Dhillon, Parinaaz Dhaliwal and Maheshwari Chauhan combining for 331 points.Raiza and Parinaaz both registered scores of 111 out of 125, while Maheshwari contributed 109 to the team total. China claimed the gold with 346 points, with Kazakhstan taking silver.The podium finish gave India another medal in shooting at the Aichi-Nagoya Games, while Meena’s historic run ensured the country’s first-ever Asian Games medal in soft tennis.India’s campaign also saw two-time Olympic medallist Manu Bhaker advance to the women’s 10m air pistol individual final. articles.title: From wanting to be a cricketer to making Asian Games history: How Jay Meena went from ball boy to India’s first soft tennis medallist
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: Jay Meena’s journey to India’s first-ever Asian Games medal in soft tennis began not with a racket in his hand, but with an interest in cricket.The 14.
articles.body: Jay Meena’s journey to India’s first-ever Asian Games medal in soft tennis began not with a racket in his hand, but with an interest in cricket.The 14-year-old who once dreamed of becoming a cricketer has now become a history-maker, securing a bronze medal after reaching the men’s singles semifinals at the Asian Games here on Wednesday. Meena’s campaign ended in the semifinals, where he went down 2-4 to Japan’s Takuya Kurosaka. The Indian lost the first three sets before mounting a spirited comeback to win the fourth and fifth sets and reduce the deficit to 2-3. However, Kurosaka won the sixth set 4-1 to seal the contest.For Meena, the path to this moment started almost by chance.After joining Pioneer Public School in Dewas, he came across a soft tennis court. Initially curious about the unfamiliar sport, he began by watching the players before helping out as a ball boy. It was only gradually that he started playing himself.What began as curiosity soon turned into a serious sporting pursuit. Meena moved through school and district competitions before progressing to the state and national levels. By the age of 14, he was already competing internationally in Japan, the home of soft tennis.From cricket dream to soft tennis breakthroughMeena established himself as one of India’s leading soft tennis players when he won the men’s singles gold medal at the 36th National Games in Gujarat in 2022. He also contributed to Madhya Pradesh’s medal-winning performances in the men’s team and doubles events.His progress continued in 2025 when he became the National Champion in men’s singles.At the 2022 Asian Games in Hangzhou, Meena reached the quarterfinals of the men’s singles event and also represented India in the men’s team competition.His international breakthrough, however, came in 2024.Partnering Aadhya Tiwari, Meena won bronze in mixed doubles at the World Soft Tennis Championships, creating history as part of India’s first-ever medal-winning pair at the event.More history before Asian Games breakthroughMeena added another landmark achievement at the Asian Soft Tennis Championships in 2025.He became the first Indian to win a medal at the continental championships after reaching the men’s singles semifinals and securing bronze. He went on to win a total of four medals at the continental event.Now, at the Asian Games, Meena has added another historic chapter to his career.His quarterfinal victory on Wednesday assured India of its first-ever Asian Games medal in soft tennis, with Meena guaranteed at least a bronze.The achievement comes during his third Asian Games appearance. A TAGG (Target Asian Games Group) athlete, Meena had previously represented India at Jakarta 2018 and Hangzhou 2022.His preparations for the latest phase of his international career included stints at National Coaching Camps in Ahmedabad and Jammu, where he trained towards the Asian Championship and Asian Games respectively.From watching soft tennis players at a school court in Dewas to becoming an international medallist and now securing India’s first Asian Games medal in the sport, Meena’s journey has taken him far beyond the cricketing dream with which it began.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Emma Raducanu inspired by Andre Agassi in plotting route back to top of tennis
articles.summary: As Emma Raducanu plots a route back to the pinnacle of tennis, the Briton is taking inspiration from Andre Agassi's 2009 autobiography.
articles.body:
As Emma Raducanu plots a route back to the pinnacle of tennis, the Briton has been taking inspiration from Andre Agassi's 2009 autobiography.

Five years have passed since Raducanu's remarkable US Open triumph, when at the age of 18 she became the first qualifier in the Open era to win a Grand Slam.

American Agassi was a teenage prodigy himself and later claimed the first of his eight major singles titles at Wimbledon in 1992 aged 22.

But between the peak years of his career, he had to overcome a challenging period when he went four years without a major and dropped to 141st in the world rankings.

"I was especially intrigued by the passage where he got out of his slump in the late 1990s by creating his own training regimen and finding his way back to the top," Raducanu told Uniqlo.

"It speaks in depth about his early successes and the lows he reached, perhaps as a result of them.

Agassi said his hope was for his experiences to help other players going through similar periods in their own careers.

"It's wonderful to hear that anybody can relate," Agassi told BBC Breakfast.

"It was literally the hope that if one person read it and it gave them hope, some tools to understand that they're not alone, they can figure it out and get to a healthier place without having to direct their frustrations at the game of tennis, then it was a success for me.

"So, hearing that 17 years later it can still impact somebody, especially in this game, it does make me feel good."

Raducanu reached a career-high ranking of 10 in July 2022, but the 23-year-old has slipped to 98th in the world.

Her progress continues to be hampered by physical issues, and she most recently missed the US Open as she continues her recovery from a stress fracture in her lower right leg.

A foot injury disrupted her pre-season training before she spent two-and-a-half months off court with a post-viral illness earlier this year.

But Raducanu enjoyed one of the best weeks of her career at Queen's Club in June, reaching her biggest final since her triumph in New York five years ago.

Agassi won all four of the sport's Grand Slams and claimed Olympic singles gold at the 1996 Games.

Asked what advice he would give Raducanu, Agassi said: "I would encourage her to focus on being the best of herself on a daily basis, but don't judge that by results or thinking that somehow you have to be 100%.

"You have to learn to be 100% of whatever percent you're at [and] be comfortable in your own identity inside of that - not what people say.

"Back in my day, I could just put down the paper and not read it. Now it seems like it's harder for these youngsters to avoid."

Keothavong 'can't fault' GB after BJK Cup loss to Czechs

GB dominate Ecuador to reach Davis Cup Finals

For Agassi, tennis was by no means a childhood passion. His father, keen for his son to become the very best, would introduce him to others as a future number one tennis player.

That additional pressure, Agassi says, led him to play with "fear". It was not until he sank from world number one to 141st that he felt able to reconnect with the sport.

Agassi, who created a foundation providing education for under-served children during that time, said: "I had more success from that point forward than I did playing out of fear.

"The first thing I would advise a parent to think about is that it's not their life, it's their child.

"You raise a child in their way and they'll never depart from it. You just have to find out what their way is."

Agassi will captain Team USA in the Laver Cup at The O2 in London later this week, between 25-27 September.

"Tennis is a hamster wheel of sorts - the fact that these guys make room in their schedule to play this incredible event tells you how great this event is," Agassi added.

"We're obviously playing Team Europe, in Europe, so I don't know where the crowd is going to have their heart.

"But I know one thing - they're going to see some spectacular tennis."

articles.title: Kazajistán - España: partidos, horario y dónde ver hoy en TV la Billie Jean King Cup
articles.standfirst: Los detalles de los cuartos del torneo
articles.summary: Los detalles de los cuartos del torneo
articles.body: La Selección Española de Tenis inicia su andadura en la Final a 8 de la Billie Jean King Cup 2026 enfrentándose a Kazajistán en la ronda de cuartos de final en Shenzhen (China). El conjunto capitaneado por Carla Suárez, formado por Cristina Bucsa, Jessica Bouzas, Sara Sorribes, Marina Bassols y la recién coronada en Sao Paulo Kaitlin Quevedo, parte como favorito a priori para certificar el acceso a semifinales. Las aspiraciones de la 'Armada' se han visto reforzadas tras confirmarse la sensible baja en el cuadro kazajo de su gran estrella y número uno del ranking WTA, Elena Rybakina. Pese a la ausencia de su principal figura, el equipo asiático mantendrá un bloque altamente competitivo liderado por la veterana Yulia Putintseva y la especialista en dobles Anna Danilina. Las jugadoras españolas buscarán romper la barrera de cuartos de final de las últimas ediciones e imponer su solidez tanto en los duelos individuales como en el hipotético punto de dobles para citarse entre las cuatro mejores naciones del torneo continental. La eliminatoria de cuartos de final entre Kazajistán y España se disputa este miércoles 23 de septiembre a partir de las 11:00 horas (horario peninsular español). La eliminatoria entre el combinado kazajo y la selección española se podrá seguir en directo por televisión e internet en España de forma gratuita a través de Teledeporte y la plataforma RTVE Play. Sigue toda la actualidad del tenis, la cobertura minuto a minuto de la eliminatoria y la última hora de la Billie Jean King Cup en MARCA.com y escucha la retransmisión en directo en Radio MARCA.
